blocks.text: Alcohols and phenols are hydroxy compounds: organic compounds with at least one hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to an aliphatic or an aryl (aromatic ring) carbon, respectively. They occur widely and have many uses. Ethanol, also called ethyl alcohol or grain alcohol, is familiar to almost everyone, and alcohols can be used as fuels; ethanol made from bio-based materials is used as a biofuel.

After Louis Pasteur's work showed that bacteria exist, surgeons began in 1867 to clean surgical instruments and wounds with phenol solutions. Because of phenol's strong antiseptic action, a patient's chance of surviving surgery rose greatly. Phenol also burns healthy tissue, however, so it was too harsh for this use, and gentler alternatives were later found. Phenol is still an ingredient of some disinfectants, such as soaps and hospital disinfectant liquids.
